theory: The strict definition requiring a value to exceed frequencies on both sides excludes plateau peaks and boundary peaks, although later teaching and accepted questions count them. Clarify that a peak can be a high region, including a plateau or boundary peak, separated from another peak by lower frequencies. The daily-rainfall example is a time-series measurement graph, not a frequency distribution of rainfall; replace that teaching figure with ordered data values and their frequencies. Restrict the general column-graph claim to meaningfully ordered values: arbitrary nominal category order cannot establish distribution peaks.
summary: Clarified plateau and boundary peaks, replaced the rainfall teaching figure with ordered values and frequencies, and restricted the general graph claim to meaningfully ordered data. Replaced the flagged genre and peak-count tasks with numerical modality classifications, removed the uniform-mode subtasks without removing whole items, updated affected structures and quiz options, and supplied the missing booklet citations while preserving all other content.
reviewSummary: All 20 practice items and seven quiz questions have correct answers and use booklet-supported distribution classification or matching tasks; every quiz has exactly one correct option and specific distractor explanations. The theory is consistent with the booklet's peak-counting convention, and no worked examples or removals were supplied.
